items.title: 67849_Leroy Elliot Stewart oral history interview
items.q: The name of this outfit was called Sonny Marshall and his Harlem Stompers.

ctx.x: No, there weren't any bands performing in Englewood. I find that, when I started playing the bass fiddle, I used to -- oh, let's see, I was about at least -- oh, 15, 16, or possibly 17, I'd say. I used to travel to other towns like Newark, and I joined a little jazz combo. And by that time I was real, real hot and heavy and playing by ear, you know. And I joined this combo. They had heard about me.

So at that time Dad had given me a little car, and I was able to get around, you know, and I was, oh, traveling doing one nighters once in a while, as far as Newark, and Passaic and around -- let's see. The name of this outfit was called Sonny Marshall and his Harlem Stompers. It's something like that. It was a small combo, you know, five, six pieces.
What, did you play for dances? You played for dances?
